paste-image-in-chat-does-not-work-1807b4.goalText: Paste image in chat does not work
paste-image-in-chat-does-not-work-1807b4.openingPrompt:
A prior PRD (865) targeting this exact title failed before any fix landed — its run errored
on a scheduler PRD-path resolution bug (see separate proposed Epic "Failed epic-scoped PRD
silently archived without running the fix") and its source PRD got archived as if the work
had shipped. It had not: the paste-image bug itself was never actually investigated or fixed.

There is no repro detail beyond the title — the original feedback item that produced PRD 865
carried no more information than "Paste Image in Chat does not work". Start by reproducing:
try pasting an image (Cmd+V from clipboard, e.g. a screenshot) into the Epic chat composer
(`EpicDetail.tsx`/`EpicComposer.tsx`) and into the Terminal tab's input, and determine where
the paste is silently dropped — clipboard read permission, a missing paste handler on the
composer's textarea/input, an unsupported image MIME type, or something else. Fix the actual
break, and add a regression test (component test for the composer's paste handler, or an e2e
test if the fix is Electron-clipboard-specific) so this doesn't regress silently again.

Done = pasting a clipboard image into the chat composer actually attaches/sends it (or shows
a clear, actionable error if images truly aren't supported yet — but confirm with the user's
intent first if that's the conclusion, since the title implies they expect it to work).

failed-epic-scoped-prd-silently-archived.goalText: Failed epic-scoped PRD silently archived without running the fix
failed-epic-scoped-prd-silently-archived.openingPrompt:
Reproduced today via job 865-paste-image-in-chat-does-not-work (sourced from Epic
psess-ms9yi6hy-14). Its PRD source lived at the epic-scoped path
session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/psess-ms9yi6hy-14/prds/865-paste-image-in-chat-does-not-work.md.
The run log
(~/.claude/session-manager/scheduled-plans/runs/2026-08-01T06-19-53-002Z/865-paste-image-in-chat-does-not-work.log)
shows:

  [scheduler] failed to read PRD: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open
  '/home/bilko/Projects/session-manager/session-manager-operations/scheduler/prds/865-paste-image-in-chat-does-not-work.md'

`prdPathForJob()` in src/main/scheduler.cjs (~line 495) resolves only the legacy flat
per-project dir via `prdDirForCwd`/`resolvePrdWriteDir` (src/main/lib/prdLocations.cjs), not
the epic-scoped dir the PRD actually lived in. `executeJob` (~line 1908-1945) does have a
fallback that calls `findPrdDir(job.slug)`, which searches `resolvePrdsDirs()` — and that
function's doc comment explicitly says it includes every project's epic-scoped PRD dirs via
`listEpicPrdDirs(cwd)`, unfiltered by recency (this was a deliberate fix for an earlier
142-PRD-across-6-quiet-projects incident). But in this run the fallback evidently still
missed the file: there's no "PRD not in project dir; found ..." log line, meaning
`findPrdDir` returned null even though the file existed on disk in an epic dir.

Net effect after the read failure: the job was recorded as failed, but the PRD source file
was later moved into session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/psess-ms9yi6hy-14/prds-archived/
(the same place completed work gets archived), and the queue.json entry for this slug is now
gone entirely — no trace in queue.json's jobs array. So a job that errored on a path-resolution
bug ends up looking exactly like a shipped one: archived PRD, no queue row, no visible failure
history. The user only found out via the scheduler completion notification for this specific
run, not via anything in the app's current state.

Investigate and fix:
1. Why `findPrdDir`/`resolvePrdsDirs` missed an epic-scoped PRD that existed on disk at fire
   time — check for a race between epic-dir creation/PRD write and job dispatch, and whether
   `allProjectCwds()` (which resolvePrdsDirs iterates) has any caching/staleness that could
   exclude a cwd or an epic dir just created moments earlier.
2. `prdPathForJob()` itself should probably resolve epic-scoped PRDs directly (the job/queue
   row likely already knows or can look up its epic id) rather than relying on a legacy-dir
   guess + best-effort fallback search — the fallback-then-fail design is exactly how this PRD
   silently ate the paste-image fix.
3. Whatever archives a failed job's PRD into prds-archived/ (instead of leaving it in prds/
   for a retry, or flagging it distinctly) needs to stop treating "PRD unreadable" the same as
   "PRD completed" — a job that never ran the actual work must not look identical to one that
   shipped it.
4. Add a regression test: an epic-scoped PRD (not the legacy flat dir) should be readable and
   fireable by the scheduler, including through the findPrdDir fallback path, and a failed
   read must leave a durable, visible failure record (queue history entry, not just a run log
   file on disk) rather than disappearing.
